a.text: 'If you deem the waves too raucous, then command the ocean to be still.'
'Civilization flourishes, the city roars forth. The only things capable of destroying them, are they themselves.'
'Do not entrust that battle to time, for they will defeat even time. Grasp that duty, for you must entrust it to yourself.'

steps.name: A Voice on the Television
steps.text: Something truly unexpected has occurred at the Major! Two championship winners have gone to the Wall of Champions together, an unprecedented event!

steps.name: A Voice on the Television
steps.text: Moreover, the Radiant Knight rejected her award from the Knights Association, and left on her own!

steps.name: A Voice on the Television
steps.text: What a blasphemous turn of events.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Ow, ow, ow...

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: Old man, if you can't fight anymore, then keep your head down. Just leave the rest to Maria and Zofia!

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Should we step outside? How dare you– Gaah! Ow, ow!

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: Why are you staring at your hammer like that, Marcin? Did ya start pining for the good ol' days after one night of exercise?

steps.name: Bald Marcin
steps.text: Maybe a bit.

steps.name: Bald Marcin
steps.text: I wonder how the Nearl family is doing.

steps.name: Maria
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Maria
steps.text: Uncle... You're leaving the Grand Knight Territory?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Are you girls even Nearls? Stop staying so much at Zofia's. It's unbecoming.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: I'll be gone for a while, so during that time... Margaret.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Are you sure you want to stay in Kazimierz?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: You should already know what you'll be up against.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Nobody will understand you.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Of course. I've always known that.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: If that's the case, then I have nothing else to say.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Why the sudden change of heart?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Toland...

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Why'd you decide to leave all of a sudden, huh? For what purpose?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: What do you see when you look at me now?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Why are you asking? You should know better than anyone else.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But to be completely honest, you've let us all down.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: You don't have to hold rank in the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi, or be the person who changes the National Council. But you should at least have been our hero, our Nearl.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I don't know where you plan on going after you leave the city, but let me say this –– you let them all down. If they see your face again, they may well decide to take your life.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Think they can beat me?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: I've given up a lot of things, Toland.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: But I still find myself often clinging to a rather idealistic sentiment.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: They should still be out there somewhere.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: He was the eldest son of a war hero. My brother, the most powerful knight in the family.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: And she... is the most beautiful woman in all of Kazimierz. Elegant and dignified, like a gemstone.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: They were my pride and joy, veritable gifts from heaven. They shouldn't have disappeared without a trace like that.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: It's been over a decade.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: I've never stopped thinking about it.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: It's already been fifteen years. After wasting all that time and effort, why are you now––

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: This is just... paid leave.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: All by yourself?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Isn't one person enough for a hopeless vacation?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: You're not the type to get swept by the emotions the Radiant Knight brought, so I won't ask why you decided to do this––

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: You know how to find me... 'Us.'

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: The one I need to find... is myself.

steps.name: Sona
steps.text: Rhodes Island, huh.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: They're able to provide you with treatment. And they won't force you to do anything.

steps.name: Sona
steps.text: Since that's the team the Radiant Knight used to play for... then I guess they're trustworthy?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Their ideals will one day illuminate this world. Even now, I still believe in them.

steps.name: Sona
steps.text: Will you ever head back there?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: ...I will, one day.

steps.name: Iwona
steps.text: Be sure to spar a few rounds with me then.

steps.name: Justyna
steps.text: I-Iwona!

steps.name: Iwona
steps.text: What? Who wouldn't want to challenge the champion?

steps.name: Greynuty
steps.text: Count me in too.

steps.name: Greynuty
steps.text: A legendary lineage of knights... Really gets you going, doesn't it?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: You have my word. I'll entertain you when the time comes.

steps.name: Sona
steps.text: Ahaha... Look at you guys, all fired up right after a tiny bit of rest..

steps.name: Sona
steps.text: You knew from the beginning you weren't one of us Infected, right?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Sona
steps.text: But you still chose to fight for us?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: I fight for the downtrodden.

steps.name: Spokesman McKee
steps.text: The Board is very upset.

steps.name: Spokesman McKee
steps.text: Looks like we'll lose a few months of bonuses.

steps.name: Spokesman Malkiewicz
steps.text: Bonuses, huh.

steps.name: Spokesman Malkiewicz
steps.text: What we did cost the lives of so many Infected, so many knights, and even the Armorless Union. All that only adds up to our bonuses?

steps.name: Spokesman McKee
steps.text: About that...

steps.name: Spokesman McKee
steps.text: Come with me, Malkiewicz. We ought to discuss where you go from here.

steps.name: Spokesman McKee
steps.text: What you said earlier about the telephone really made sense, after I had some time to mull it over.

steps.name: Spokesman Malkiewicz
steps.text: Whose call are we waiting for?

steps.name: Spokesman McKee
steps.text: A newsman's.

steps.name: Spokesman Malkiewicz
steps.text: Hm... a newsman? Do we have to sit for an interview?

steps.name: Spokesman McKee
steps.text: They call him that. It's just a title.

steps.name: Spokesman Malkiewicz
steps.text: Wait a sec... Newsman? You can't mean–

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: McKee?

steps.name: Spokesman McKee
steps.text: It's me. Let me first introduce you to the person on the other end of the phone. He is the chairman of the Rose Paper Union, 'The Newsman' Kain.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Malkiewicz is here too.

steps.name: Spokesman Malkiewicz
steps.text: Yes, it's an honor to speak to you.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: I paid good money to buy Malkiewicz from Mieszko Industries. He will be my right-hand man.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: In other words, there are no strangers among us, McKee. You can call me 'father.'

steps.name: Spokesman McKee
steps.text: Yes, father.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Good, how's your mother doing?

steps.name: Spokesman McKee
steps.text: Very well, father. She thinks of you often.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: And what about you? Are you married yet?

steps.name: Spokesman McKee
steps.text: I... Not yet, I'm afraid.

steps.name: Spokesman McKee
steps.text: How are you, father? Where are you right now?

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Columbia.

steps.name: Spokesman McKee
steps.text: When will you come back to Kazimierz?

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Haha... It's not time for that yet, McKee.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Those short-sighted idiots don't see the truth, but Columbia is the real enemy that threatens Kazimierz.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Our newspapers have yet to cover their city, and our voices have yet to reach Columbian ears.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: The speed of their development is frightening, and we must move to contain them... to seize their markets.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: The games between countries are most fascinating, McKee.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: But, those... Nobles. Bah. So rigid in their ways... Victoria, Ursus. These powerful countries are so ignorant that one cannot help but feel for them

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Malkiewicz.

steps.name: Spokesman Malkiewicz
steps.text: Yes!

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Are you willing to give everything for the General Chamber of Commerce?

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: You are a capable person. I can tell, just from reading a few words of your report.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Could it be that you still... harbor compassion for those knights?

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Seems like I hit the mark.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Child, let me pose you a question.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: When the number of Kazimierz's attack ships far exceeds that of Ursus, when Columbia is flooded with Kazimierzian caravans and goods, when our border strongholds more than double in number––

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Will that be the end of war? Would Ursus still threaten us? Would Kazimierz still be weak?

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: The knights are the true parasites on Kazimierz. Imbeciles barking for glory. Nobles? Bah.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: I heard about what happened at the Major. Does the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi think they've 'protected their honor?'

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Honor and glory. Give them as much of it as they want.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: The time, and the people, are on our side. After a few more tournaments, the masses will forget about the shockwaves brought by the Radiant Knight, and return to invest in the next round of consumption and entertainment.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: For them, arguing over 'which knight is stronger' and 'whether knight merchandise is fairly priced' is more important than looking after the dregs we leave behind.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: The country stands on our side. Kazimierz is already inextricably tied to the economic foundations laid by the K.G.C.C. Those pitiful campaign knights... Look how many have already voluntarily surrendered to us.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Malkiewicz.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: This time, you have the right to choose.

steps.name: Spokesman Malkiewicz
steps.text: Before I answer, can I first ask a question?

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Please do.

steps.name: Spokesman Malkiewicz
steps.text: Mr. Czarny... Because he failed to prevent the Radiant Knight from entering the arena, he was exiled... By my standards, this is unacceptable.

steps.name: Spokesman Malkiewicz
steps.text: Why did it happen?

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Oh, Mr. Czarny. I see, the turning point in your destiny, Malkiewicz. I ought to thank him too.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: However, what if I told you Mr. Czarny's disappearance–– was not directly related to the Radiant Knight incident?

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: What if I told you that his exile was just a consequence of a longstanding series of power struggles, and an excuse finally being found to take him out of the picture?

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: ––Czarny was exiled by political opponents over a bribery incident a few years ago.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: It had nothing to do with the Radiant Knight... It had nothing to do with your destiny. More often than not, this is the truth of the world. The truth of modernity is one of supreme indifference.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Come, Malkiewicz.

steps.name: A Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Let us become the voice of this world.

steps.name: Platinum
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: What? Not a fan of our new storefront?

steps.name: Platinum
steps.text: Storefront? You're... opening a shop?

steps.name: Monique
steps.text: Are you blind?

steps.name: Platinum
steps.text: No... But, hand sanitizer?

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: Origi-Cloud Daily Wares has been the most popular brand in recent years––

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: ...and there are 'three bosses' behind the company that launched Origi-Cloud Daily Wares.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: Soon, those three bosses will become a part of the General Chamber of Commerce.

steps.name: Platinum
steps.text: You guys...

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: Yes, but it's just for the sake of joining them.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: As you know, the more inside information we have, the more we'll know about the direction the winds blow in the future.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: Sooner or later, mercenaries and assassins will become obsolete. There's no need for so many of them, and in the end, all they're good for is killing. Them, on the other hand, they can take over a country.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: This is another crossroads of our time, Platinum.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: By the way, why don't you come be our poster girl, since we're missing a clerk anyway? You're very good-looking. It'll be perfect.

steps.name: Monique
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: During an upcoming mission for the Union, the three of us will 'vanish,' then we'll find the best plastic surgeon, swap faces, and become by-the-books businesspeople.

steps.name: Platinum
steps.text: So... you took advantage of the blackout caused by the Infected... to kill everyone with connections between the Board and the Union.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: They deserve the credit for making it so easy.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: The Board can't stop fighting with itself, under the table or otherwise.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: Whoever controls the Union holds an overwhelming advantage–– and no director dared to blatantly manipulate it, or let others do so.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: It is precisely because of this tacitly agreed restraint that they ended up losing control of the Union.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: Haha, let me tell you a joke. The people of Kazimierz no longer know the name or whereabouts of the person leading the organization they hire for their hitjobs.

steps.name: Platinum
steps.text: Does Darksteel really exist?

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: Who knows?

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: Darksteel might be a single person, maybe two. Darksteel might even be a front, or just refer to the signals us Lazurites use during operations.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: But for all you know, Darksteel might've passed you on the street, or be sitting in a board meeting, or on vacation in a Sami villa.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: Nobody knows. And that's why the name strikes fear.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: One last thing. Whatever the case, you should've been a damned woman. Condemned as a scapegoat.

steps.name: Roy
steps.text: We'll have our eyes on you. You're Armorless too. Surely you wouldn't want to make enemies of us, right?

steps.name: Platinum
steps.text: (I... have to run...)

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Doctor, Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Oh, Nearl.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: The reason I called you here is...

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: If Rhodes Island ever calls for me, then I shall head to your side. Doctor, Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Great!

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: I've been a drifter for many years. It isn't until now... that I've finally had the time to look back at my old home.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Maybe I should go visit my grandfather's grave...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Nearl.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Oh, Doctor, let's give them some space.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Nearl, take care of yourself!

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Of course. Godspeed.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: It's time for us to part ways as well, Nearl.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: ...Shining.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Actually, I...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: It's alright. I know what you're going to say.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We will return to Londinium. Just as you've returned here.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: The past... and those sins. We'll excise them ourselves.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Shining?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz... You might really come to hate me at some point.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: But, trust me, I will always stay by your side.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I... How could I ever hate you?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: If that time comes, and you ever need me––

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: I swear to you––

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: ––that the Radiant Knight, Margaret Nearl, will fight for you both.

a.text: The lights of Kawalerielki shine brightly once more, as do the lights throughout the General Chamber.
Like the answer smeared across the city by humankind.
The curtains of night slowly begin to lift.
That is how civilization continues to flourish.

steps.text: Three days later, in a certain village outside the Grand Knight Territory...

steps.name: Sona
steps.text: This is the place?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Quaint little town, isn't it?

steps.name: Sona
steps.text: Do you always come stay out here?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I used to stay at a more classic den of thieves. Even if I had my eyes on other cities, I did most of my work underground and in the black market.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But then... I met some people. They changed the way I saw things.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I'll skip to the important part though. A bit after that, we fought a battle with the Rusthammers. Know those guys? A bunch of lunatics.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Many people have the wrong idea about the Rusthammers, that they're just a band of thieves. But they aren't. During that battle, I saw kids, teenagers, swinging metal pipes.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Pretty crazy, huh?

steps.name: Sona
steps.text: Yeah... Sounds scary.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: That is what makes 'em truly scary.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: The Rusthammers weren't born to fight against civilization. They were born of the development of civilization.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Don't expect them to have some end goal in mind, or some greater purpose. It's a mistake to treat them like a group of rational actors––

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: They're just the orphans of civilization. They were born when it moved on, but couldn't bring everyone along.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Homeless, with nowhere to go, forced to survive in the barren wilderness littered with Originium. They are the Catastrophes.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Thanks to them, we've become united, and as a result, we've also realized a few things...

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: That we don't want to end up like those lunatics.

steps.name: Sona
steps.text: So? What are we gonna do?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I want you to meet a few people.

steps.name: Sona
steps.text: What kind of people?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: A few Infected.

steps.name: Sona
steps.text: Infected?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: A few farmers, a few knights.

steps.name: Sona
steps.text: A real melting pot, huh.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: A few manual laborers, a few bounty hunters.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: A few village chiefs unable to make ends meet, a few worn-out nobles.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: A few college students, a few illiterates.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: A few people trying to change Kazimierz. A few people who were changed by Kazimierz.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Don't be surprised already. The real surprise has only just begun.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Sona, you've asked me before, what's the point of thwarting the General Chamber. What's the point of the knights.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I'd like to pose the same question back to you. Before the rise of the merchants, before Kazimierz was firmly in the grasp of the General Chamber of Commerce––

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: ––who was it that exploited the poor and oppressed the masses? Who hanged the Infected, while hiding inside the massive edifices erected by and to their power?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: The knights.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: We don't prop up the reality of a villain just beacuse there isn't one now. Why bother though? We always lose out in the end.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But to be honest, though you rarely hear the words 'General Chamber of Commerce' spoken without curses attached... even a broken clock is right twice a day.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: The people who've been left behind by the city should unite.

steps.name: A Haggard Girl
steps.text: Toland, is this...?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: An Infected knight from the Grand Knight Territory. We've formed a working relationship.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Are the others here?

steps.name: A Haggard Girl
steps.text: Yes, they're all inside...

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Good. Why don't you head inside as well, Clore......

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: It's nearly light out.
